reasoning_traces.think:
The system employs a two-stage pipeline: first, a temporal transformer-based TAAD extracts per-player action logits from video frames, leveraging attention mechanisms to capture temporal dependencies beyond static frame classification. This is followed by a denoising sequence transduction (DST) model that uses these logits along with game-state features to generate structured event sequences. The key innovation lies in introducing per-player attention within DST, allowing it to reason about individual player dynamics rather than treating all players uniformly. Additionally, architectural diversity among DST models enables robust ensembling through agreement-based voting, improving generalization. The temporal transformer in TAAD enhances performance by projecting features into a higher-dimensional space and applying stacked transformer layers with pre-norm ordering, which supports long-range temporal reasoning. Training modifications correct a learning rate bug, ensuring stable convergence. These components form a coherent mathematical framework for soccer action spotting, grounded in attention-based neural architectures and ensemble theory.
